JUDGEMENT CALL / UNRESOLVED - the bottom rail y~950:
  The drafter's bottom rail is drawn with a failing pen. A column-by-column scan of the darkest pixel in y in [935,975] gives ink at x=440-460 (y 955-956), a 10px patch at x=504-513 (y 956), nothing 461-503 or 514-543, then x=544-627 (y 954-959), nothing 628-689, then strong ink x=690-744 (y 946-950) into V-DC#11's bottom lead. The y-trend is one smooth curve, so the DRAWING almost certainly intends a single rail from the left rail all the way to the 15V source. However, taking it as continuous puts BOTH terminals of V-DC#11 (15V) on one net - a dead short - because 11.0 is already tied through row 765 -> col 400 -> S44 -> the bottom rail, all in solid unambiguous ink (S37, S44, S39 are all clean solid Ts, individually verified in pixel dumps). Per rule 1 of the brief (electrical impossibility wins) I placed the break at the one place where the ink genuinely disappears and is weakest: the x~461-543 stretch, which has only a single 10px scrap of pencil across 84px, whereas the x~628-689 stretch is flanked by ~50px of strong dark ink and is bridged. Result: n7 = {C#12 bottom, V-DC#11 bottom}, a sane 2-terminal return node. The alternative reading (fully continuous rail) merges n7 into n3 and short-circuits the 15V source; the other alternative (cutting at S44) would mean denying a clean solid T. THIS IS THE ONE PLACE IN THIS IMAGE WHERE I OVERRODE THE INK, and it is the least certain call here. CAVEAT FOR THE REVIEWER: circuit_249, annotated in the same batch, contains a V-DC source that is short-circuited in completely unambiguous solid ink (a plain-wire rung tying two columns together through a solder dot), which proves this dataset's generator does emit shorted sources. That makes the ink-faithful alternative here - one continuous bottom rail, merging n7 into n3 and accepting the 15V short - a live possibility rather than an absurdity. I went with the break because (a) it is the only reading that satisfies the ERC-clean requirement, (b) unlike circuit_249 the connection in question is NOT drawn in ink - it has to be asserted across an 84px stretch that holds only 10px of pencil - and (c) the brief ranks electrical impossibility above the ink prior. If the reviewer prefers the ink-faithful reading, the single change is to replace the merge ['11.1','12.1'] with ['2.1','12.1'] and ['2.1','11.1'].
  Residual warning: I-DC #8 still has both terminals on n3. That is forced by unambiguous solid ink and involves no judgement call - row 595 reaches the bottom rail through col 250 below S27, and row 765 reaches it through col 400 below S37; both verticals are plain wires with no component on them. The drawing really does put a wire in parallel with the 10A source.
